title: Zero to Recruiter: a Talent Acquisition roadmap
subtitle: Learn recruiting in Lagos, one step at a time. Plan about 5 hours a week. Free resources come first; paid options are marked.

stages.title: Stage 1: What recruiters do
stages.description: Learn the hiring process from workforce planning to onboarding, and where recruiters work with hiring managers.
outcomes: Trace hiring from workforce planning to onboarding
Compare agency and in-house recruiter roles
Use clear criteria instead of gut feel

resources.title: The HR Learning Lab: HR Essentials (video playlist)
resources.duration: 1 hour for starter lessons and notes
resources.why: Learn what HR does, then see where recruiting fits in the employee life cycle.
resources.action: Watch lessons 1–4. Sketch the employee life cycle and mark where recruitment fits.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-27: public HR Essentials playlist, 16 listed videos; description and initial lesson titles readable without sign-in. The fetch also exposed a YouTube error banner, so playback and mobile app handoff remain untested. Content developed by Dr. Heather Staples; videos produced using AI-supported tools. This is introductory study, not a professional qualification.
resources.access_summary: Public playlist; no sign-in to read. Playback untested. AI-assisted, introductory content.

milestones.label: Watch lessons 1–4. Sketch the employee life cycle and mark where recruitment fits.

resources.title: The HR Learning Lab: Talent Acquisition (video playlist)
resources.duration: About 2 hours for selected lessons and notes
resources.why: Get the key terms and a quick tour of job analysis, sourcing, selection and hiring.
resources.action: Watch the first five lessons. Draw the hiring process in your own words.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-27: public Talent Acquisition playlist, 43 listed videos, description and lesson titles readable without sign-in; playback and mobile app handoff not tested. Creator discloses AI-supported production; confirm consequential claims against primary sources.
resources.access_summary: Public playlist; no sign-in to read. Playback untested. AI-assisted; check key claims.

milestones.label: Watch the first five lessons. Draw the hiring process in your own words.

stages.focus: Map the hiring lifecycle and name the recruiter's job.
stages.practice: Draw the hiring lifecycle from workforce planning to onboarding and label who owns each step.
stages.effort_note: This includes a one-hour HR Essentials starter budget; use selected lessons, not both full playlists.

stages.title: Stage 2: Fair hiring basics
stages.description: Learn fair hiring, job requirements, selection steps and the rules for candidate data in Nigeria.
outcomes: Follow a fair hiring process
Separate job requirements from person specifications
Handle candidate data with care

resources.title: Human resources: recruitment and selection
resources.duration: About 12 hours for the full course; assigned sections 4.2–4.5 only
resources.why: See how job analysis leads to a job description and person specification.
resources.action: Read sections 4.2–4.5. Draft a job analysis, job description and person specification for a Lagos vacancy. Tie each criterion to the work.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the official OpenLearn course page: the course text is free and its sections can be opened without signing in. A free account is needed to track progress, access all quizzes and activities, and claim the free Statement of Participation. Course content was last updated in 2018 and uses UK equality-law framing; pair it with the Nigerian sources in Stage 7.
resources.access_summary: Free to read without sign-in. Account for quizzes and the free participation statement. Older UK-law examples; use Nigerian sources too.

milestones.label: Read sections 4.2–4.5. Draft a job analysis, job description and person specification for a Lagos vacancy. Tie each criterion to the work.

resources.title: BUS301: Human Resource Management
resources.duration: About 5 hours for assigned Units 2–3; about 24 hours for the full course
resources.why: Review staffing plans, job analysis, interviews, tests and offers through readings, videos and practice.
resources.action: Complete Units 2–3: readings, videos and practice. Skip the other units.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the official BUS301 page and Saylor FAQ: no tuition or fees; a free account is required to enroll; course materials and the course-completion certificate are free, subject to completing the course requirements. U.S. employment-law material is not Nigerian law.
resources.access_summary: Free course and certificate; account needed to enroll. U.S. law examples, not Nigerian law.

milestones.label: Complete Units 2–3: readings, videos and practice. Skip the other units.

resources.title: Recruiting, Hiring, and Onboarding Employees
resources.cost: Full course not confirmed free; paid options
resources.duration: About 20 hours for the full course
resources.why: Covers workforce planning, job analysis, sourcing, selection, hiring metrics and onboarding.
resources.action: After the free stages, check whether a preview or no-certificate option is available. Confirm trial and billing terms before enrolling; free access is not confirmed.
resources.access_note: NOT confirmed free for the full course. Checked 2026-10-26 on the course page and Coursera Help Center: “Enroll for free” does not establish permanent free access. The page lists inclusion with Coursera Plus (a paid subscription); the course FAQ says course materials are available through paid Certificate access, a free trial, or Full Course, No Certificate where available. A Coursera account may be required to enroll or use a preview; no account-free full-course route was verified. Coursera Help says previews for most courses are limited to the first module and provide no certificate; Full Course, No Certificate is offered only for selected courses. I could not confirm that this course offers that option. A free trial is temporary, not proof of ongoing free access; the course-specific duration, post-trial billing/cancellation terms, and Nigeria checkout price were not verified. Financial aid is mentioned in the FAQ. Eligibility and course-specific coverage were not confirmed; it is not counted as free. Treat as paid/conditional, not confirmed free. Prices vary by region and promotion.
resources.access_summary: Full-course access is not confirmed free. A preview may cover only module 1; Plus and certificates are paid. Trial terms and Nigeria pricing are unverified.

milestones.label: After the free stages, check whether a preview or no-certificate option is available. Confirm trial and billing terms before enrolling; free access is not confirmed.

stages.focus: Run a full and fair recruitment and selection process.
stages.practice: Write a one-page fair-process checklist for a small Lagos employer hiring its first employee.
stages.effort_note: The 14-hour figure is a planning allowance for the selected OpenLearn sections, Saylor Units 2–3 and practice; the full 20-hour Coursera course is optional and not included. Do not add full-course estimates together.

stages.title: Stage 3: Define the role
stages.description: Define the work and what success looks like before you source candidates.
outcomes: Turn a vague request into a job description
Set clear hiring criteria before interviews
Build a scorecard for every interviewer

resources.title: O*NET OnLine: occupation tasks, skills and knowledge
resources.why: Set role requirements from the work, not from another job advert.
resources.action: Search O*NET for your practice role. Pick five duties to check against Nigerian job ads.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the official O*NET homepage: public occupation search and profile information opened without a sign-in or payment prompt. Account: not required for the public database. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. The classifications and labour-market data are U.S.-based, not Nigerian requirements.
resources.access_summary: Free public database; no account needed. U.S. data, not Nigerian requirements.

milestones.label: Search O*NET for your practice role. Pick five duties to check against Nigerian job ads.

resources.title: Recruiter job description (free public sample)
resources.why: See how a recruiter role summary, duties and requirements fit together.
resources.action: Compare the sample with a Lagos vacancy. Keep supported requirements and mark each essential or desirable.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on Workable’s Recruiter job-description page: the sample text is publicly readable without payment or sign-in. Account: not required to read. Form: none shown for the sample. Trial: Workable advertises a separate 15-day software trial for posting jobs; it is not needed to study or adapt the sample. Certificate: none offered. The template is generic and should be localised.
resources.access_summary: Free sample; no sign-in to read. The 15-day software trial is separate and not needed.

milestones.label: Compare the sample with a Lagos vacancy. Keep supported requirements and mark each essential or desirable.

resources.title: Structured hiring: Introduction (free worksheets)
resources.why: Learn the six steps of structured hiring, starting with clear success criteria.
resources.action: Download the worksheet. Build a scorecard for your practice role with up to six criteria.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on Greenhouse Support: the six-step structured-hiring article is readable and links two direct PDF downloads. Account: not required. Form: none shown for the article or downloads. Trial: none needed; Greenhouse software is a separate product. Certificate: none offered. The method is product documentation but transfers to other hiring systems.
resources.access_summary: Free article and two PDFs; no account or form. The method works beyond Greenhouse.

milestones.label: Download the worksheet. Build a scorecard for your practice role with up to six criteria.

stages.focus: Write a job description and a scoring scorecard before sourcing.
stages.practice: Produce a job description, a person specification and a six-attribute scorecard for one real vacancy.

stages.title: Stage 4: Find candidates
stages.description: Find candidates, write clear outreach and treat people well throughout hiring.
outcomes: Write Boolean searches for a real role
Compare referrals, job boards and direct search
Plan outreach and candidate updates

resources.title: Boolean search cheatsheet: Google operators for sourcing
resources.duration: About 1–2 hours to adapt and practise
resources.why: Use search operators to find candidates by role, skill and location.
resources.action: Write three Boolean strings for a Lagos role. Test with dummy terms; do not collect real CVs or personal data.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the individual Workable cheat sheet and its public index: the article and PDF link are readable without payment, sign-in or a content form. Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: a separate 15-day Workable hiring-software trial is advertised in the page footer; it is not needed to use the cheat sheet. Certificate: none offered.
resources.access_summary: Free article and PDF; no sign-in or form. The software trial is separate.

milestones.label: Write three Boolean strings for a Lagos role. Test with dummy terms; do not collect real CVs or personal data.

resources.title: Talent Sourcing Strategies (video 16)
resources.why: Compare sourcing options such as referrals, job boards, pipelines and job fairs.
resources.action: Watch the video. Pick two channels for a small Lagos employer and explain why.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the public YouTube video page: 6:34, with description and transcript accessible without payment or sign-in. Account: not required for this public listing. Form: none. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. The creator discloses AI-supported production; playback was not tested, and this is an overview rather than a primary authority.
resources.access_summary: Public video and transcript; no sign-in or payment. Playback untested. AI-assisted overview.

milestones.label: Watch the video. Pick two channels for a small Lagos employer and explain why.

resources.title: How to create a positive experience for candidates
resources.why: Plan clear candidate updates, interview preparation and respectful decisions.
resources.action: Draft a first-contact message and an update plan for a Lagos role. Include interview prep and delay updates.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work guide (updated March 2026). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. The examples describe Google’s own practice, not Nigerian law or a guarantee of outcomes.
resources.access_summary: Free guide; no account or form. Google examples, not Nigerian law or guaranteed results.

milestones.label: Draft a first-contact message and an update plan for a Lagos role. Include interview prep and delay updates.

stages.focus: Build Boolean strings and a candidate experience plan.
stages.level: Beginner; a defined practice role from Stage 3 assumed.
stages.practice: Compare job boards, referrals, pipelines and direct search for the practice role; build three Boolean strings and a short outreach message, then add a simple candidate-update plan.

stages.title: Stage 5: Screen and shortlist
stages.description: Use job criteria to shortlist fairly before you speak with candidates.
outcomes: Screen CVs against the scorecard
Ask everyone the same job-related questions
Record clear reasons for each decision

resources.title: OpenLearn section 4.10: Shortlisting
resources.modality: Free written course section and activity
resources.cost: Free to read; account for course extras
resources.why: Practise comparing candidates against a job specification.
resources.action: Read section 4.10 and do its shortlisting activity. Give one job-related reason per choice; check your assumptions.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the direct OpenLearn section page: the section and activity instructions are readable without signing in. Account: a free account is needed to enrol, save progress, use course activities/quizzes and claim the free Statement of Participation; it is not needed to read this section. Form: account creation only. Trial/payment: none. Certificate: optional free Statement of Participation, not a professional qualification. The course uses older UK examples; use Stage 7 for Nigerian legal material.
resources.access_summary: Free to read without sign-in. Account for course activities and the free participation statement. Older UK examples; use Nigerian sources too.

milestones.label: Read section 4.10 and do its shortlisting activity. Give one job-related reason per choice; check your assumptions.

resources.title: Screening Candidates (video 24)
resources.why: Review screening steps from CVs to references.
resources.action: Watch the video. Draft five phone-screen questions tied to job criteria. Use fictional records; do not judge protected or irrelevant traits.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the public YouTube page: the 8:14 listing and transcript were accessible without payment or sign-in. Account: not required for this public listing. Form: none. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. Playback was not tested. The creator discloses AI-supported production; the transcript mentions U.S. federal/state rules, which are not Nigerian legal guidance.
resources.access_summary: Public video and transcript; no sign-in. Playback untested. AI-assisted; U.S. law is not Nigerian guidance.

milestones.label: Watch the video. Draft five phone-screen questions tied to job criteria. Use fictional records; do not judge protected or irrelevant traits.

stages.focus: Shortlist against criteria and record defensible evidence.
stages.level: Beginner to intermediate; a scorecard from Stage 3 assumed.
stages.practice: Screen ten fictional practice CVs against your Stage 3 scorecard, record one evidence line per decision, then draft five consistent job-related phone-screen questions.

stages.title: Stage 6: Interview and decide
stages.description: Ask job-related questions and score answers against a shared rubric.
outcomes: Write behavioural and hypothetical questions
Set clear examples for scoring answers
Run a mock interview and compare scores

resources.title: A guide to structured interviewing for better hiring practices
resources.why: Learn to set criteria, write interview questions and score answers consistently.
resources.action: Write eight questions: four behavioural and four hypothetical. Link each to your Stage 3 scorecard and add poor and strong answer examples.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work guide (updated March 2026). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. The guide’s examples and internal results are Google-specific; use the method, not its metrics as local guarantees.
resources.access_summary: Free guide; no account. Google examples and results are not local guarantees.

milestones.label: Write eight questions: four behavioural and four hypothetical. Link each to your Stage 3 scorecard and add poor and strong answer examples.

resources.title: Effective interviewer training for better candidate experiences
resources.why: Give useful feedback with evidence and leave time for candidate questions.
resources.action: After the mock interview, rewrite your notes with evidence so another person can follow your decision.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work guide (updated March 2026). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. It is guidance, not a formal interviewer qualification.
resources.access_summary: Free guide; no account. Guidance, not a formal qualification.

milestones.label: After the mock interview, rewrite your notes with evidence so another person can follow your decision.

stages.focus: Ask structured questions and score against a written rubric.
stages.level: Intermediate; a scorecard and interview questions assumed.
stages.practice: Run a 30-minute mock interview with a friend, score it independently, then compare your scores.

stages.title: Stage 7: Offers, onboarding and Nigerian law
stages.description: Learn the basics of offers, onboarding, data protection and employment law in Nigeria.
outcomes: Explain why candidate data needs a lawful basis
Draft a short privacy notice
Know when to check the law or ask a lawyer

resources.title: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023: General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025
resources.why: Learn the data-protection rules recruiters meet when they handle CVs and references.
resources.action: Read Articles 15, 16, 17, 18, 27, 33 and 34. Draft a six-line privacy notice for a job application.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by opening the official NDPC PDF: the document is publicly readable without an account, form, trial or payment; no certificate is offered. I checked its arrangement of articles and opening provisions, not every assigned article or the whole directive. It is regulatory guidance, not legal advice; confirm current law with a Nigerian lawyer.
resources.access_summary: Public NDPC PDF; no sign-in or payment. Only opening provisions checked. Not legal advice.

milestones.label: Read Articles 15, 16, 17, 18, 27, 33 and 34. Draft a six-line privacy notice for a job application.

resources.title: Labour Act, Chapter L1 Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004
resources.provider: PLAC Laws of Nigeria (statute copy); ILO NATLEX listing
resources.why: Review recruiting rules and the written terms employers must give workers.
resources.action: Read sections 7, 23, 24, 25, 26 and 71. Write three questions to ask before sourcing for an employer.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by opening the public PLAC PDF: no account, form, trial or payment is required; no certificate is offered. This is an official-style reproduction, not a government gazette. The Labour Act dates from 1971/Cap. L1 LFN 2004 and may have been amended or partly superseded; verify current law and seek Nigerian legal advice before acting.
resources.access_summary: Public PLAC copy; no account or payment. Not a government gazette; the law may have changed. Ask a Nigerian lawyer.

milestones.label: Read sections 7, 23, 24, 25, 26 and 71. Write three questions to ask before sourcing for an employer.

resources.title: A data-driven approach to optimizing employee onboarding
resources.why: Use new-hire check-ins to spot gaps in tools, skills and support.
resources.action: Draft a 30-day onboarding checklist. Give each item an owner and check-in date.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work page (August 2025). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. The examples describe Google’s own programme; adapt the approach to a Lagos employer.
resources.access_summary: Free guide; no account. Google examples; adapt them for a Lagos employer.

milestones.label: Draft a 30-day onboarding checklist. Give each item an owner and check-in date.

stages.focus: Handle candidate data and offers under Nigerian rules.
stages.level: Intermediate; the full hiring process from Stages 1 to 6 assumed.
stages.practice: Draft a candidate privacy notice and a 30-day onboarding checklist.

stages.title: Stage 8: Tools, metrics and job search
stages.description: Bring your work together, track hiring metrics and apply for junior roles in Lagos.
outcomes: Track a practice hiring pipeline
Show one hiring project in a portfolio
Apply with evidence, not just certificates

resources.title: Managing Your Contacts With the HubSpot CRM
resources.why: Use a free CRM as a simple stand-in for an applicant tracking system.
resources.action: Create a free Academy account. Add ten fictional candidates to the free CRM, track their stages and count the funnel. Never upload real candidate data.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the lesson page and HubSpot CRM product page. Study: the lesson is explicitly free (four videos, 20 minutes). Account: a free Academy account is required; the signup form collects account details and the page states that product updates/promotional emails may be sent. Form: account creation only, no separate lesson form. Trial/payment: the CRM free tier is described as non-expiring and requires no credit card; paid tiers exist but are not needed. Certificate: none is advertised for this lesson.
resources.access_summary: Free 20-minute lesson; Academy account needed. The CRM tier does not expire or need a credit card; paid tiers exist.

milestones.label: Create a free Academy account. Add ten fictional candidates to the free CRM, track their stages and count the funnel. Never upload real candidate data.

resources.title: HR Metrics That Support Hiring Decisions (video 43)
resources.why: Learn key hiring measures, including time to fill and selection ratio.
resources.action: Watch the video. Note the selection-ratio and time-to-fill formulas, then calculate stage conversions in your fictional pipeline.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the public YouTube page: the 4:19 listing and transcript were accessible without payment or sign-in. Account: not required for this public listing. Form: none. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. Playback was not tested. The creator discloses AI-supported production; use the definitions as a primer and verify consequential decisions against primary sources.
resources.access_summary: Public video and transcript; no sign-in. Playback untested. AI-assisted primer; verify key decisions with primary sources.

milestones.label: Watch the video. Note the selection-ratio and time-to-fill formulas, then calculate stage conversions in your fictional pipeline.

resources.title: The Hire Standard: Fall 2026 U.S. recruiting benchmarks
resources.why: See how hiring funnel rates vary by company size in a U.S. case study.
resources.action: Read the summary and funnel tables. Note how rates vary by company size, then calculate your practice-pipeline rates.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on Greenhouse’s report page and direct PDF. Study: the provider advertises free access and the direct PDF opened without account, payment or a submitted form; the landing page has a free-access/download CTA. Account: not required for the direct file. Form: no form submission was needed at the PDF URL. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. Data covers U.S. organizations using Greenhouse through August 2026 and is not a Nigerian benchmark.
resources.access_summary: Free direct PDF; no account or form. U.S. Greenhouse customer data through August 2026, not a Nigerian benchmark.

milestones.label: Read the summary and funnel tables. Note how rates vary by company size, then calculate your practice-pipeline rates.

stages.focus: Track a pipeline, report funnel numbers, build a portfolio.
stages.level: Beginner to intermediate; a completed practice project assumed.
stages.practice: Assemble a portfolio folder: job analysis, advert, scorecard, Boolean strings, screening notes, interview kit and funnel numbers. Then apply to five junior recruiter or HR assistant roles.
